definition.definition: Gross value added is output minus intermediate consumption, measured at basic prices. At constant prices it is valued at the prices of the base year (2022-23), so a change reflects a change in volume rather than in prices. MoSPI publishes a Total Gross Value Added row together with its industry break-up in the National Accounts Statistics, quarterly and annually; the total is reproduced here as published, and the year-on-year figure on this page is computed from those published levels and labelled as computed.
definition.source_name: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) — National Accounts Statistics
definition.term: Gross Value Added (GVA) at basic prices, constant prices

indicator.label: GVA growth, y-o-y (computed)
indicator.scoring_rule: Computed from published constant-price levels, not a published growth rate. Green 5-8%, watch 3-5% / >8%, red <3%.
indicator.source: MoSPI NAS quarterly (computed from published levels)
indicator.status_reason: 8.2% - above-trend growth - check whether it is a base effect

cross_checks.note: The published figure is quoted on the headline; the index-derived series is the long history drawn on the chart. The index is published rounded to one decimal, so a computed y-o-y carries a quantisation of about +/-0.05pp.
